cards.title: Defer or Lazy-Trigger App Scripts to Shield Core Assets
cards.summary: Move non-visible app scripts out of the initial load, then inject them on user interaction so they no longer block store rendering.
cards.use_when: Speed tests flag unused jQuery/app JavaScript that loads in the first second even though the app's widget is not visible, and you still need the app for later interaction (e.g. reviews, SMS).

cards.title: Assess Whether Each Blocking Script Is Visible or Pixels
cards.summary: Triage blocking JavaScript by asking whether the script needs to run in the first second, and cut or delay the ones that don't.
cards.use_when: Google speed tests flag unused JavaScript / 'reduce unused JavaScript' on your home, collection or product page and you need to decide which scripts to keep, defer or remove.

cards.title: Clean Residual Scripts After Uninstalling Apps
cards.summary: Uninstalling an app leaves its scripts in theme.liquid, head.liquid and footer.liquid — remove each residual tag to reclaim speed.
cards.use_when: You have removed or no longer use an app (or plugin) but its assets may still be loading and slowing your Shopify store.

cards.title: Right-Size Images and Pick the Correct Format
cards.summary: Shrink product/hero images and choose JPEG/PNG/MP4 by need rather than uploading DSLR originals.
cards.use_when: Speed tests show images are too large for mobile, or your store's pages load slowly because of oversized image assets.

cards.title: Use lazy-sizes for Bulletproof Image Lazy Loading
cards.summary: Trade the SRC for an empty pixel plus a data-src and lazy-load class, then let lazy-sizes swap in the real image.
cards.use_when: You want stronger lazy loading than the native loading='lazy' attribute gives, e.g. for a slide-out drawer or list of images below the fold.

cards.title: Font Loading: Add font-display: swap
cards.summary: Large custom font files block text rendering — font-display: swap lets a default font show immediately.
cards.use_when: Your theme uses multiple custom fonts and speed tests show text-rendering delays or layout shifts caused by font loading.

cards.title: Defer and Async Scripts to Prioritize Core Assets
cards.summary: Add defer/async to non-critical scripts so hero images and core assets download first.
cards.use_when: You control script tags in theme.liquid and want app/plugin scripts to stop delaying core asset loading.

cards.title: Delay Non-Visible CSS with media-onload-Print
cards.summary: CSS for elements not visible at load can be applied after the page loads, reducing render-blocking time.
cards.use_when: Large CSS files reference elements below the fold and your store's CSS is blocking rendering.

cards.title: Evaluate Speed-Apps and Optimization Vendors Skeptically
cards.summary: Speed optimization apps are not the answer and some vendors use tricks that help the score but not real users.
cards.use_when: You are considering buying a speed-optimization app or hiring a speed specialist for your Shopify store.

cards.title: Check Page Vitals Before Trusting Them
cards.summary: Passing vitals (LCP/CLS) does not guarantee a good speed score — validate all three key pages.
cards.use_when: Your home page shows 'all vitals passed' and you're deciding whether store speed is genuinely healthy, or you're auditing a store for the first time.

cards.title: Reproduce the Original Page-Speed Audit Method
cards.summary: A repeatable pass: inventory apps, cut blocking JS, size images, fix CSS, and test home/collection/product pages.
cards.use_when: You're running a full speed audit of your own Shopify store for the first time and need a consistent sequence of steps.

cards.title: Understand the Three Core Web Vitals and Their Thresholds
cards.summary: The three Core Web Vitals metrics—LCP, FID, CLS—and the specific thresholds you should chase on every product and landing page.
cards.use_when: Setting performance targets for your storefront's key templates (homepage, category, PDP, checkout) before or during a speed optimization project.

cards.title: Diagnose LCP Bottlenecks with the Network Waterfall
cards.summary: Use the browser Network tab waterfall to find the wide-bar assets delaying Largest Contentful Paint.
cards.use_when: When your homepage, category page, or PDP loads slowly and you need to identify which specific asset is the LCP bottleneck.

cards.title: Optimize LCP: Compress, Serve via CDN, Unblock Rendering
cards.summary: Four mechanical levers for pulling Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 seconds on storefront pages.
cards.use_when: After you've identified your LCP element and need concrete fixes for your hero image, category tiles, or above-the-fold content.

cards.title: Make the LCP Element Explicit with Preload and Fetchpriority
cards.summary: Resource-priority hints that ensure the browser fetches your hero content before lower-priority assets.
cards.use_when: When a hero product image or above-the-fold headline loads late because the browser is guessing wrong about priority.

cards.title: Reduce product-page interaction delay by cutting JavaScript execution
cards.summary: Diagnose and reduce delayed responses to store controls using INP and interaction profiling.
cards.use_when: When customers click add-to-cart, filters, or quantity controls and experience noticeable lag before the page responds.

cards.title: Prevent CLS with Explicit Image Dimensions and aspect-ratio
cards.summary: Reserve layout space for images and embeds so late-loading content doesn't shove your layout and cause accidental taps.
cards.use_when: When category grids, PDP images, or ingredient/spec elements jump as they load, causing mis-taps or a broken-feeling storefront.

cards.title: Use the Web Vitals Chrome Extension to Name the Exact Problem Element
cards.summary: Google's Web Vitals extension logs the specific DOM elements and subpart timings behind poor LCP and CLS in the browser console.
cards.use_when: When Lighthouse gives you a numeric score but you need to know which actual element on your homepage or PDP to fix.

cards.title: Run Site-Wide Audits in Parallel with Unlighthouse
cards.summary: One command audits every URL on your domain in parallel, surfacing outlier pages that drag down sitewide performance.
cards.use_when: When your store has hundreds or thousands of URLs (product, category, and content pages) and manual per-page auditing is impossible.

cards.title: Use Lighthouse Scores to Triage, Not to Judge Vendors
cards.summary: How to interpret popular-site performance comparisons and avoid cargo-culting someone else's scores.
cards.use_when: When deciding which performance targets are realistic for your store, or when a stakeholder points at a competitor's high score.

cards.title: Prioritize speed fixes by financial impact and conversion benchmarks
cards.summary: Maps ecommerce speed benchmarks and revenue math to help operators justify and sequence performance work.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest engineering time in site speed, or building a business case for a performance sprint before a peak sales period.

cards.title: Use asset_url to force Shopify CDN cache refresh
cards.summary: Explains how Shopify's asset_url filter appends version numbers so the CDN serves updated CSS/JS instead of stale files.
cards.use_when: After editing theme CSS or JavaScript and finding browsers or the CDN still serve an old version of the asset.

cards.title: Deduplicate Liquid forloops to cut server execution time
cards.summary: Guides Shopify developers to find and remove repeated theme loops that crawl the same collection data multiple times.
cards.use_when: Auditing a Shopify theme's performance or after multiple developers have worked on the same theme and page rendering feels heavy.

cards.title: Audit and remove third-party apps slowing your Shopify store
cards.summary: Shows how app scripts enter the theme head via content_for_header and how to decide whether an app's value justifies its speed cost.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a bloated app stack or evaluating whether to install one more app on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Unblock HTML parsing with defer and async on script tags
cards.summary: Explains parser-blocking scripts and the specific defer/async fix, with a before-and-after code example.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing slow first render where the browser appears to stall before showing content on a Shopify or any site.

cards.title: Compress and resize images with correct Shopify size parameters
cards.summary: Covers image weight (50-75% of page), lossless compression tools, correct size requests, sprites, and empty image sources.
cards.use_when: Optimizing page weight across product, collection, or landing pages where images dominate load time.

cards.title: Replace standard YouTube embeds with lite embeds
cards.summary: Explains why standard video iframes bloat pages and how lite embeds cut nearly a megabyte by loading the player on click.
cards.use_when: A product page, landing page, or homepage uses YouTube or similar video embeds and load time is a concern.

cards.title: Remove or defer Quick View pop-ups on collection pages
cards.summary: Details how Quick View can pre-load full product page data for dozens of thumbnails and how to detect or replace it.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a Shopify collection or category page that feels slow or bounce-prone, especially on mobile.

cards.title: Cut pop-ups and hero sliders that add page weight
cards.summary: Sets parameters for pop-up timing and slider count so experiential elements don't sabotage load speed.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a homepage or landing page where promo pop-ups and rotating hero carousels are slowing load.

cards.title: Clean up redirects, broken links, and use 301s correctly
cards.summary: Covers how redirect chains and broken assets add HTTP requests and how to consolidate them on Shopify.
cards.use_when: Doing a technical SEO or speed audit of store navigation, collection URLs, or after replatforming or renaming products.

cards.title: Apply lazy loading to below-fold content
cards.summary: Explains how lazy loading defers off-screen content until visible, with a concrete example of its effect.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a product page, collection, or homepage that loads many images, reviews, or carousels up front.

cards.title: Consolidate tracking tags with a tag management system
cards.summary: Explains using Google Tag Manager to reduce many tracking JavaScript requests into one, as a speed measure.
cards.use_when: A store loads multiple analytics, conversion, and retargeting tags and page speed is suffering, or you need to disable a failing tag quickly.

cards.title: Run and interpret website speed tests with the right expectations
cards.summary: Explains PageSpeed Insights, GTmetrix, and Pingdom differences and how to read Core Web Vitals metrics.
cards.use_when: Establishing a speed baseline before optimization work, or verifying the impact of changes.

cards.title: Optimize mobile checkout with Shop Pay and mobile-first speed
cards.summary: Argues checkout is often overlooked in speed work and cites Shop Pay's higher mobile checkout-to-order rate.
cards.use_when: Improving mobile conversion on the path from cart to order, where shoppers abandon due to checkout delays.

cards.title: Research hosting and platform capacity for peak traffic events
cards.summary: Frames platform/hosting scale as a precondition for speed work, with questions to ask before BFCM-style spikes.
cards.use_when: Preparing a store for a major sales event or choosing an ecommerce platform/hosting plan.

cards.title: Measure Perceived Performance With Slow-4G Throttling
cards.summary: Test real-user loading experience in Chrome DevTools by throttling to slow 4G or 3G with cache disabled, rather than chasing a perfect PageSpeed score.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether your product or landing page actually loads acceptably for real shoppers before or after a speed optimization pass.

cards.title: Set loading=eager Above the Fold and lazy Below
cards.summary: Control image loading priority with the loading attribute so above-fold hero/logo images load immediately while below-fold images defer.
cards.use_when: Optimizing image loading order on a homepage, PDP hero, or landing page where above-fold images must appear fast and off-screen images shouldn't block.

cards.title: Fix CLS With Explicit Width and Height Attributes
cards.summary: Eliminate cumulative layout shift by hardcoding width and height attributes matching the exact rendered size so the browser reserves layout space.
cards.use_when: Fixing a red CLS score or content jumping on load on your homepage, PDP, or landing page.

cards.title: Convert and Resize Images With AVIF at 2x Rendered Size
cards.summary: Shrink image files by converting to AVIF and resizing intrinsic dimensions down to 2x the rendered size, keeping retina sharpness at a fraction of the file weight.
cards.use_when: Reducing image payload on image-heavy pages such as homepage heroes, product galleries, or landing pages.

cards.title: Audit Loaded Assets With a Waterfall Chart
cards.summary: Find unnecessary JavaScript and CSS by reading a request waterfall to spot scripts (jQuery, unused WooCommerce files) loaded on pages that don't need them.
cards.use_when: Reducing render-blocking resources on a landing page or homepage before deeper optimization.

cards.title: Dequeue jQuery for Logged-Out Front-End Users
cards.summary: Remove jQuery bloat from public pages by dequeuing and deregistering it only for logged-out users on the front end, keeping it for admin.
cards.use_when: Trimming render-blocking scripts on public pages where jQuery is confirmed unused but WordPress loads it by default.

cards.title: Unload Unused WooCommerce Assets Per Page With Asset CleanUp
cards.summary: Surgically remove unused WooCommerce CSS/JS (and other plugin assets) from pages that don't use them, while leaving them active where they are needed.
cards.use_when: A landing page or content page loads WooCommerce or other plugin assets it never uses, slowing first paint.

cards.title: Unload Default WordPress Bloat for Logged-Out Users
cards.summary: Disable unused WordPress defaults such as emojis, Gutenberg block CSS, dashicons for guests, and pingbacks through builder/theme performance settings.
cards.use_when: Establishing a fast baseline on any WordPress storefront before page-specific fixes.

cards.title: Self-Host Google Fonts as WOFF2 to Cut External Requests
cards.summary: Download Google Fonts, convert to WOFF2, and serve them locally to remove the external font-request dependency.
cards.use_when: Reducing third-party font requests and render-blocking on your storefront, especially where fonts are used site-wide.

cards.title: Verify Caching and Compression via Response Headers
cards.summary: Confirm gzip compression and server caching are actually active by inspecting response headers in the Chrome Network tab.
cards.use_when: Checking whether your host's caching and compression are enabled, or verifying after you turn them on.

cards.title: Sequence WordPress Speed Work: Fundamentals Before Caching
cards.summary: Fix images, asset loading, and fonts before enabling compression, caching, or a CDN, since infrastructure alone won't fix heavy resources.
cards.use_when: Planning a speed project for a storefront or landing page and deciding what to prioritize.

cards.title: Interpret Waffling Speed Test Scores and Average Runs
cards.summary: Trust scores only after repeated runs, since tools like PageSpeed Insights fluctuate, and cross-check against perceived performance.
cards.use_when: Compiling speed data for a decision or report and deciding whether your score is trustworthy.

cards.title: Apply the WordPress Speed Optimization Checklist
cards.summary: A portable checklist covering image loading, dimensions, file format, asset unloading, local fonts, and caching/compression.
cards.use_when: Running a structured speed pass on any WordPress storefront or landing page.

cards.title: Compare Optimized vs Unoptimized Page Under Throttling
cards.summary: Reproduce the genuine before/after by loading an optimized page and a non-optimized copy in an incognito window on slow 4G with cache disabled.
cards.use_when: Validating that a speed optimization effort actually changed the real loading experience, not just a lab score.

cards.title: Do Not Lazy-Load Background Images; Optimize Them Instead
cards.summary: CSS background images can't use the loading attribute, so shrink their files with modern formats instead of deferring them.
cards.use_when: Tuning a hero or section background image that must cover an area but is slowing the page.

cards.title: Resize Images to 2x Rendered Size for Retina
cards.summary: Match intrinsic image dimensions to 2x the rendered size so retina screens stay sharp without loading oversized originals.
cards.use_when: Selecting export dimensions when optimizing product photos, hero images, or gallery images for a storefront.

cards.title: Add Alt Text and Preserve It When Copying Image Settings
cards.summary: Use the image optimization pass to add alt text to every image, and remember copy/paste of element settings can overwrite existing alt text.
cards.use_when: Standardizing image accessibility and SEO metadata while optimizing page images.

cards.title: Founder Ad = Founder's Argument, Not Raw Footage
cards.summary: A founder ad is a structured presentation of the founder's argument across three story elements, not simply video of the founder talking.
cards.use_when: Planning a founder-led ad concept for a Meta acquisition campaign and deciding what the ad actually needs to communicate.

cards.title: Highest-Performing Founder Script Structure
cards.summary: The source's strongest founder script sequence runs Claim, Proof of Claim, Unique Mechanism tied to founder story, Proof of Mechanism, CTA plus social proof.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing the body script for a founder-led video ad before shooting.

cards.title: Hooks Should Target Viewer Desire, Not Founder Narrative
cards.summary: Effective hooks speak to the viewer's underlying desire or problem; hooks that only narrate the founder's personal story underperform.
cards.use_when: Writing hook variants for a founder video ad or diagnosing why a founder ad has weak thumb-stop rate.

cards.title: Batch-Shoot Modular Creative for Volume
cards.summary: Pair many hooks with a few core body scripts to scale creative volume efficiently from a single shoot day.
cards.use_when: Planning a founder video shoot and deciding how many assets to produce per session.

cards.title: Concept Diversification via Founder Script Roles
cards.summary: Move the founder out of the standard first-person protagonist role into witness, interviewer, or reader roles to create genuinely different ad concepts.
cards.use_when: Your founder ads all feel the same and you need distinct concepts without changing the offer or product.

cards.title: The Founder Involvement Spectrum
cards.summary: Vary how much of the founder appears — from full protagonist to completely absent — to extend creative range and reduce format fatigue.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to involve the founder in the next creative batch, especially when shoot time or talent budget is limited.

cards.title: Editing Dynamics to Avoid Format Fatigue
cards.summary: Vary camera angles, scenery, and edit dynamics across founder videos so repeated exposure does not fatigue the format.
cards.use_when: Founder videos are still running but performance is declining and you need to refresh without changing the core concept.

cards.title: Match Founder Ads to Stage of Awareness
cards.summary: Founder content should be built for a specific stage of awareness, and the claim, mechanism, and proof mix should shift accordingly.
cards.use_when: Mapping a founder ad set to cold versus warm audiences or diagnosing why a founder ad works in one placement but not another.

cards.title: Founder ads present an argument, not a founder monologue
cards.summary: Reframe founder ad production as scripting the founder's argument around the viewer's problem rather than filming a founder talking about themselves.
cards.use_when: Planning a founder-led video shoot or briefing a script for paid social acquisition creative.

cards.title: Highest-performing founder ad script structure: claim, proof, mechanism, CTA
cards.summary: Use the Claim → Proof of Claim → Unique Mechanism (founder story) → Proof of Mechanism → CTA/Social Proof sequence identified from top-spending founder ads.
cards.use_when: Drafting the body script for a founder video ad for cold acquisition traffic.

cards.title: Batch-shoot founder ads: pairing hooks with bodies
cards.summary: Multiply one shoot into dozens of ads by combining multiple hooks with a few distinct body scripts rather than shooting ads one by one.
cards.use_when: Scheduling a founder shoot and deciding how much creative volume to generate from one session.

cards.title: Founder face is a sameness signal: diversify concept and format
cards.summary: Repeated talking-head founder ads fatigue because the founder's face creates sameness; fix with true concept diversification plus format and scene variation.
cards.use_when: A founder ad has started to fatigue and you are deciding what to shoot next.

cards.title: Use portfolio theory: never let founder ads carry the whole account
cards.summary: High-performing founder ads can generate enormous revenue but also decay; keep other formats alive instead of overweighting one concept.
cards.use_when: Deciding budget allocation across creative formats after a founder ad becomes a top spender.

cards.title: Founder involvement spectrum: protagonist, voice, evidence, proxy, absent
cards.summary: Choose how much of the founder appears in each ad — face, voice only, evidence, proxy, or fully absent — to create format diversity from the same script.
cards.use_when: A founder is camera-shy, time-constrained, or you need format diversification without new concepts for paid social.

cards.title: Change the founder's role in the script to multiply concepts
cards.summary: Move the founder between protagonist, witness, interviewer and reader roles to generate materially different scripts from the same story.
cards.use_when: You need new founder ad concepts without new founder stories, especially on smaller teams that cannot pay creators.

cards.title: Founder ad concept matrix: persona × awareness × angle × offer × proof × role
cards.summary: Generate founder ad concepts systematically by varying six variables to address different buyer types with matching proof.
cards.use_when: Building a new batch of founder ad concepts and deciding who each ad targets and what offer it carries.

cards.title: Static vs renewable founder story elements
cards.summary: Separate founder story components that must stay consistent from those you can refresh weekly to keep producing new ads.
cards.use_when: Planning ongoing founder ad production and deciding what to source and script each month.

cards.title: Run founder ad production as a collection pipeline
cards.summary: Treat founder content as a monthly production system: hoard raw customer and supplier material continuously, then script and shoot in concentrated blocks.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ongoing founder ad cadence with limited founder time.

cards.title: Founder video production quality rules
cards.summary: Founder ads must be edited like real ads — dynamic cuts, overlays, relevant hooks, natural delivery and varied scenes — not raw talking head uploads.
cards.use_when: Preparing a founder shoot and post-production for paid social creative.

cards.title: Hook variation: 2–4 per body, up to 8, never 30
cards.summary: Keep hook variations per founder body in the 2–4 range (up to about 8) so testing budget is not spread too thin.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many hook variants to launch per founder ad body in a paid social test.

cards.title: Run founder ads through the founder's handle as partnership ads
cards.summary: Running founder ads via the founder's account rather than the company page usually performs better, with the lift tied to the founder's existing relevant content.
cards.use_when: Choosing placement and ad account identity for founder video ads.

cards.title: Founder ads are optional, and your exit terms may care
cards.summary: Founder ads can improve performance at any size, but they are a content type rather than a necessity, and heavy dependence on the founder's face can complicate an exit.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in founder-led creative or in other channels and formats.

cards.title: Differentiate a commodity product through the founder's story
cards.summary: When the product category is saturated and undifferentiated, reposition via the founder's specific problem and mechanism instead of competing on the product itself.
cards.use_when: Developing ad angles for a commoditized product where every competitor advertises the same mechanism.

cards.title: Decide Between Founder Handle and Company Page for Partnership Ads
cards.summary: Choose where to run founder-led paid social based on which page has relevant content volume and whether you want brand or person association.
cards.use_when: Deciding which ad account/page identity to run founder creative from on Instagram/Meta for an ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Three Elements of the Dishwashing-Sheet Founder Ad
cards.summary: A high-performing founder ad combined a negative hook, fast pacing, and showing the product working in the first three seconds.
cards.use_when: Writing or storyboarding a cold-audience founder ad for a consumable ecommerce product.

cards.title: Use Format Innovation to Stop the Scroll
cards.summary: Running an ad in a format the audience has never seen before stops the scroll because viewers wonder what the content is.
cards.use_when: Planning creative concepts for cold-audience ecommerce acquisition when standard founder-to-camera formats are fatiguing.

cards.title: Sequence an Ad as Hook, Curiosity Gap, Objection Handling, Benefits
cards.summary: A strong founder ad can be built in a deliberate sequence: credibility hook, curiosity gap, warehouse social proof, objection handling, then benefits over features.
cards.use_when: Scripting a founder product ad for an ecommerce brand, especially a supplement or food product with a common objection.

cards.title: Problem-Agitation Arc Ending in Scarcity
cards.summary: A contrarian hook followed by escalating problem agitation across alternative solutions, then a founder story and scarcity close, made a protein-jerky ad work end to end.
cards.use_when: Writing acquisition creative for a food or supplement brand entering a category with entrenched but flawed incumbents.
